'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian Civil War]]
***[[Syria missile strikes (January 2021)]]
****[[Israel]] carries out a wave of [[airstrike]]s on [[Syria]]'s eastern [[Deir ez-Zor Governorate]], near its [[Iraq–Syria border|border]] with [[Iraq]]. The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]] reports that 57 people have been killed and 28 others injured in at least 18 Israeli airstrikes, saying that several [[Iran]]ian arms depots were hit. A senior [[U.S. intelligence]] official says that the air raids were carried out with "intelligence provided by [[federal government of the United States|the U.S.]]" [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/mid-east/intense-israeli-airstrikes-kill-23-in-eastern-syria (''Daily Sabah'')]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**Pro-[[François Bozizé]] forces attack the [[Central African Republic]] capital of [[Bangui]], with fighting reported on multiple fronts, according to [[List of heads of government of the Central African Republic|Prime Minister]] [[Firmin Ngrébada]]. A [[Reuters]] witness reports explosions and helicopters circling over the city. The attack is successfully repelled by the [[Central African Armed Forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-centralafrica-security/rebels-attack-central-african-republics-capital-idUSKBN29I0ZI (Reuters)]
**A [[Rwanda Defence Force]] peacekeeper is killed in a rebel attack, according to [[United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic|MINUSCA]] officials. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/14/c_139666640.htm (Xinhuanet)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Three [[Ivory Coast|Ivorian]] [[United Nations|UN]] [[United Nations peacekeeping|peacekeeper]]s are killed and six others wounded in a [[jihadist]] [[ambush]] on their vehicle in central [[Mali]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210114-three-ivorian-un-peacekeepers-killed-in-mali-attack (France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Mayor of New York City|Mayor]] [[Bill de Blasio]] announces that [[New York City]] will end all contracts with the [[Trump Organization]] claiming that [[President Donald Trump]]'s incitement of "an insurrection against the U.S. government clearly constitutes criminal activity." [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/13/nyregion/nyc-trump-golf-carousel-ice-rinks.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[George Floyd protests in Australia]], [[List of name changes due to the George Floyd protests]]
**Dairy company [[Saputo Inc.|Saputo]] announces that [[Coon cheese]], its brand of [[cheddar cheese]] in Australia, will be rebranded as "Cheer" cheese, in response to a 20-year campaign by [[indigenous rights]] activist [[Stephen Hagan (author)|Stephen Hagan]] to remove the usage of the word "Coon", in reference to a [[racial slur]]. The new branding will be released in July. [https://manilastandard.net/news/world-news/344298/australian-cheese-rebrands-after-20-year-racism-battle.html (AFP via ''Manila Standard'')]
*Spanish [[telecommunication]]s company [[Telefónica]] announces that it will sell its [[cell site]]s in Europe and Latin America, which are owned by its subsidiary [[Telxius]], to American company [[American Tower]] for an estimated [[Euro|€]]7.7 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]9.4 billion). [https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/economy/telefonica-sells-mobile-phone-masts-in-europe-latin-america-for-77-bn-euros.phtml (''Buenos Aires Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[Sudanese Air Force]] helicopter crashes shortly after taking off in [[Sudan]]'s [[Al Qadarif (state)|Al Qadarif]] state, near the border with [[Ethiopia]], with the three-person crew surviving the crash, according to officials. [https://www.trtworld.com/africa/sudan-s-military-helicopter-crashes-near-border-with-ethiopia-43217 (TRT World)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
*****[[President of Indonesia|President]] [[Joko Widodo]] receives the first dose of the [[CoronaVac|vaccine candidate]] developed by [[Sinovac Biotech]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/indonesia-jokowi-gets-first-dose-sinovac-china-vaccine-covid-19-13943982 (CNA)] 
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 11,278 new cases and 306 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 858,043 confirmed cases and 24,951 deaths. [https://m.cnnindonesia.com/nasional/20210113144321-20-593180/tambahan-rekor-positif-covid-11278-kematian-tertinggi-306 (CNN Indonesia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq]]
****[[Prime Minister of Iraq|Prime Minister]] [[Mustafa Al-Kadhimi]] imposes [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic|travel and entry bans]] on 20 countries reported to have [[Variants of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|new variants]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/14/c_139665570.htm (Xinhua)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Government of Japan|government]] expands the [[state of emergency]] to seven [[Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]]s, including [[Aichi Prefecture|Aichi]], [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], and [[Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto]], as the [[Japan|country]] surpasses 300,000 cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/japan-widens-virus-emergency-areas-cases-surge-75217042 (ABC News)]
****[[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Yoshihide Suga]] announces the suspension of business travel agreements with 11 countries and regions and also restricts entry for all non-resident foreign nationals beginning tomorrow in an attempt to reduce the spread of [[COVID-19]]. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Spotlight/Coronavirus/Japan-to-suspend-entry-of-all-nonresident-foreign-nationals (Nikkei Asia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]]
****[[Jordan]] begins a [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccination]] campaign, with priority given to [[Health professional|healthcare workers]], people with chronic illnesses, and those over the age of 60. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1791926 (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] reports 115 new cases in the past 24 hours, the largest single-day total in more than five months, bringing the nationwide number of confirmed cases to 87,706. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/china-reports-115-new-coronavirus-cases-biggest-increase-in-five-months (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7|Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports their first case of a new variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] from the [[United Kingdom]] in a person who travelled from the [[United Arab Emirates]] to [[Quezon City]] on January 7 and later tested positive. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/01/13/21/ph-detects-new-covid-variant-doh (ABS-CBN News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]], [[Lineage B.1.351|501.V2 variant]]
****[[Taiwan]] reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from [[South Africa]] in a [[Eswatini|Swazi]] man in his 30s who was diagnosed with COVID-19 on January 1. [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4101209 (''Taiwan News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] reports a record 3,362 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 239,587. [https://www.thenationalnews.com/uae/health/coronavirus-highest-covid-19-cases-to-date-as-uae-records-3-362-infections-1.1145445 (''The National'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Norway]]
*****[[Monarchy of Norway|King]] [[Harald V of Norway|Harald V]], Queen consort [[Sonja of Norway|Sonja]] and [[Princess Astrid, Mrs. Ferner|Princess Astrid]] receives the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. [https://people.com/royals/king-harald-queen-sonja-norway-receive-coronavirus-vaccine/ (''People'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Turkey]]
*****[[Turkey]] approves the emergency use of the [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by [[Sinovac Biotech]]. [https://apnews.com/article/turkey-china-coronavirus-pandemic-coronavirus-vaccine-ac68dcf62293e0cc70942a1c218681a8 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Belgium]] reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from [[South Africa]] in a person from [[West Flanders]] with no travel history. [https://www.vrt.be/vrtnws/nl/2021/01/13/van-ranst-zuid-afrikaanse-variant/ (VRT)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports records for both daily counts of new cases and deaths, with 10,556 new cases and 156 deaths, bringing the nationwide cumulative totals to 507,108 confirmed cases and 8,236 deaths. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/317_DGS_boletim_20210113.pdf (DGS)]
****[[Prime Minister of Portugal|Prime Minister]] [[António Costa]] announces that stricter [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown measures]] to reduce the spread of COVID-19 will begin on January 15. There will be more exceptions to the new restrictions than there were during the first national lockdown in March and April 2020. [https://expresso.pt/coronavirus/2021-01-13-Novo-confinamento.-A-lista-de-tudo-o-que-vai-fechar.-E-as-52-excecoes-com-hoteis-mas-nao-centros-de-explicacao--que-sairam-a-ultima-hora- (''Expresso'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] reports a record 38,869 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,176,089. [https://www.elmundo.es/ciencia-y-salud/salud/2021/01/13/5fff3b1021efa060448b4695.html (''El Mundo'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports a record 1,564 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 84,767. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-55653161 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City]]
****[[Pope Francis]] and Pope Emeritus [[Benedict XVI]] receive their firsts doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] on the first day of the vaccination campaign in the [[Vatican City]].  [https://www.foxnews.com/world/pope-francis-coronavirus-vaccine-vatican (Fox News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mississippi]]
*****[[Governor of Mississippi|Mississippi Governor]] [[Tate Reeves]] receives his first dose of the [[vaccine]] live on [[Facebook]]. [https://apnews.com/article/public-health-mississippi-phil-bryant-health-coronavirus-pandemic-42ebd8b96c735d760e2ccee1d7841a6e (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[New Mexico]] reports their first case of a new [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant of SARS-CoV-2]] in a man in his 60s who traveled to the [[United Kingdom]] in December and later tested positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://kutv.com/news/coronavirus/first-case-of-coronavirus-variant-discovered-in-new-mexico (KUTV-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]], Variant of Concern 202012/01
****[[Wisconsin]] reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.cbs58.com/news/covid-19-variant-1st-found-in-uk-now-detected-in-wisconsin (WDJT-TV)]
***The U.S. surpasses 23 million cases of COVID-19, just four days after surpassing 22 million cases. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/13/health/us-coronavirus-wednesday/index.html (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[Supreme Leader (North Korean title)|Supreme Leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]]'s sister, [[Kim Yo-jong]], criticizes [[South Korea]] over their tracking of a [[military parade]] that will be held in [[Pyongyang]] during the weekend, defining South Korean officials as a "weird group, hard to understand" and the "idiot and top of the world's list in misbehaviour". [[President of South Korea|South Korean President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] says his position to establish talks with [[North Korea]] remains unchanged. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/north-korean-leader-kim-jong-uns-sister-kim-yo-jong-calls-south-korean-officials-idiot-report-2351605 (NDTV)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
***American Olympic gold-medal swimmer [[Klete Keller]] is charged with participating in the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/klete-keller-capitol-riot/ (CBS News)]
***Robert Keith Packer, a [[Virginia]]n known for wearing a "Camp Auschwitz" sweatshirt, is arrested for storming the Capitol. Additionally, former [[Rocky Mount, Virginia]] police officers Thomas Robertson and Jacob Fracker are also arrested. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/legal-issues/camp-auschwitz-sweatshirt-arrest/2021/01/13/9f98c1ae-55b0-11eb-a08b-f1381ef3d207_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[Proud Boys]] supporter Eduard Florea is arrested in [[New York (state)|New York]] for threatening to lead an armed caravan to [[Washington, D.C.]] Additionally, Florea also threatened the life of [[United States Senate|Senator-elect]] [[Raphael Warnock]]. [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/crime-and-courts/fbi-proud-boys-fan-stockpiled-ammo-knives-in-ny-home/2830111/ (WNBC-TV)] [https://www.foxnews.com/us/fbi-nyc-proud-boys-member-online-posts-us-capitol-riot-dc (Fox News)] [https://www.nydailynews.com/new-york/nyc-crime/ny-queens-proud-boy-arraigned-20210113-topip3eyj5br5lr4yndeensfha-story.html (''The New York Daily News'')]
*[[Capital punishment in the United States]]
**Shortly after midnight, the [[Federal government of the United States|federal government]] [[capital punishment|executes]] Lisa Marie Montgomery by [[lethal injection]] for the 2004 [[murder of Bobbie Jo Stinnett]], after the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] vacated the last stay on her execution. Montgomery is the first woman to be executed by the federal government since 1953. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-executions/us-executes-first-woman-on-federal-death-row-in-nearly-seven-decades-idUSKBN29I0GR (Reuters)] 
*Aftermath of the [[poisoning of Alexei Navalny]]
**Opposition politician and anti-corruption activist [[Alexei Navalny]] announces that he will return to [[Russia]] on Sunday, despite risks of being incarcerated upon his return. Navalny says that the charges against him are "fabricated". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-politics-navalny/russia-is-my-country-despite-risks-kremlin-critic-navalny-to-fly-home-idUSKBN29I0W3 (Reuters)]
*[[Flint water crisis]]
**Former [[Governor of Michigan|Michigan Governor]] [[Rick Snyder]] is charged with two counts of willful neglect of duty in connection with the [[Flint, Michigan|Flint]] water crisis, which left residents with contaminated water and a [[Legionnaires' disease|Legionnaires]] outbreak. [https://apnews.com/article/health-michigan-flint-rick-snyder-54755694e7655cc122567010e6ce26a6 (AP)] [https://www.businessinsider.com/former-gov-rick-snyder-faces-charges-over-flint-water-crisis-2021-1 (''Business Insider'')]
*Rioting erupts overnight in the [[Belgium|Belgian]] capital [[Brussels]] following the death of a 23-year-old black man in [[Law enforcement in Belgium|police]] custody, who was reportedly arrested for violating local COVID-19 restrictions. A police station was set on fire in north of the city, and [[Philippe of Belgium|King Philippe]]'s vehicle was attacked while travelling through the area. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-55656138 (BBC News)] [https://www.euronews.com/2021/01/13/death-of-young-black-man-after-brussels-arrest-to-be-probed-by-judge (Euronews)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Second impeachment of Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] impeaches [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] for "[[sedition|incitement of insurrection]]". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-55656385 (BBC News)]
**After being impeached, Trump releases a video statement from the [[White House]] condemning the rioters who [[2021 United States Capitol attack|stormed]] the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-13/trump-condemns-capitol-violence-after-house-impeachment-vote (Bloomberg)]
*[[Corruption in Estonia]]
**[[Prime Minister of Estonia|Prime Minister]] [[Jüri Ratas]] announces his [[resignation]] after the Prosecutor General suspected his [[Estonian Centre Party]] of "criminal involvement" in an [[influence peddling]] scandal involving businessman [[Hillar Teder]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/estonian-pm-resigns-over-corruption-probe-on-his-party (''Daily Sabah'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Social media use by Donald Trump|Donald Trump on social media]], [[Censorship by Google]]
**[[Google]]-owned [[YouTube]] says that it has suspended [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s account from uploading new videos or [[live streaming]] content for the next seven days, and may extend the suspension, saying that the channel had violated its rules over [[incitement to violence]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-55643774 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
**[[English people|English]] cricketer and [[all-rounder]] [[Moeen Ali]], who tested positive for COVID-19 ten days ago, confirmed that he was infected with a new variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]], which makes this the first case of the UK variant in [[Sri Lanka]]. [https://m.timesofindia.com/sports/cricket/news/englands-moeen-ali-infected-with-new-uk-strain-of-virus/amp_articleshow/80255019.cms (''The Times of India'')]
